### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `991f0dcb38e3c2ae8aa11a26e08b3374e1ba50d3` — the merge of head `cee768517a17627f30bb3b63145bb271a5238a55` into base `6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 991f0dcb38e3c2ae8aa11a26e08b3374e1ba50d3 && git checkout 991f0dcb38e3c2ae8aa11a26e08b3374e1ba50d3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0 cee768517a17627f30bb3b63145bb271a5238a55 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0 && git merge --no-ff cee768517a17627f30bb3b63145bb271a5238a55

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cee768517a17627f30bb3b63145bb271a5238a55`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: no export, signature, schema key, error code or route is added, removed or renamed. `actionHoldersOnOwnerKeyOf` is module-private and `overlaySlotBinding` stays private. Right.
- Changed answers, `action` only: `getPackageScopedItem`, `getEnvironmentScopedItem` and everything that reads them through `resolveActionByPackage` now bind a package-less action by the ADR-0150 D4 key (package, owning object, name), not by name alone. Right: D4's index table keys an action by `objectName:name` plus package, and D3's "package-less row over a package-held name is a customization" is stated over that key.
- One holder on the same owner key: still that holder's customization. Two or more holders on the same owner key: still no package's item and no environment item. Both unchanged, both right.
- No holder on its owner key: the environment's own item. A caller with no package resolves it; a package caller is refused naming the environment. Right, this is D3 (a) as written. It is a runtime resolution and authority answer, not a published accept set, so it does not make the declaration a narrowing.
- Two or more holders, none or one on its owner key: answered per owner key where the name-only count gave no binding. Right under D4; the refusal for two holders on one owner key is intact.
- Every other metadata type keeps the one-holder reading: the branch is `type === 'action'` and nothing else moves. Right.
- `packageScopedHoldersOf` is unchanged for every type: a package-less item never added a holder, before or after.
- The check-runs on this head: 56 runs, 36 success, 20 skipped, none failed or pending.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — right. Nothing in the published contract surface widens or is exposed; the diff pulls the registry's binding back to the identity ADR-0150 D4 already declares. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: no key, accepted value or requirement an author can write changes, and the rest of the tree already reads a package-less action on another object as the environment's. `@objectstack/objectql: patch` matches `none` on the one package the diff moves; `packages/runtime` changes a test file only and needs no entry. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No card and no dev report are among this review's inputs, so there are no dev flags or `open_questions` to answer. The hand-off comment's notes are answered here.
- The hand-off says the order names advisories. This seat cannot read advisories; the review judged the tree and the rule the PR states, nothing else.
- "The other files the order listed change no door answer and were left untouched; the remaining fail-closed gap goes to the owning seat as a follow-up": outside this diff and not judged here. It stays owed by `security#1`.
- Overlap with open PR #33621: confirmed, its `registry.ts` hunks sit in other regions of the file and share none with this diff.
- For the lane seat's ACCEPT of the prose remainder: the changeset and PR body say a route that names no package "answers as before". The doors that read this binding outside the diff (the by-name, exact-address and environment-address metadata reads, and the object-less action judge) follow it, so that sentence holds for the pinned compositions and should be read as scoped to them. Detail is with the seat.
- Runtime authority behaviour changes, so the human-floor approval and the queue guard stay whole-PR, as the tier rule says.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: none. Implementing file `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, read against `action-package-addressing.ts`, `action-governance.ts`, the core resolver and ADR-0150 on `main`.

- `overlaySlotBinding`: the package-less branch counts, for `action`, only the holders `actionHoldersOnOwnerKeyOf` returns, then applies the same none / one / several ladder. The stamped branches are untouched. Holds.
- `actionHoldersOnOwnerKeyOf`: the owner key is `standaloneActionOwnerKey`, with every object-less spelling folded to `GLOBAL_ACTION_OBJECT_KEY`. This is the same test `actionOwnerScopedRegistry` applies, so the binding and the owner-scoped view agree on what "same owner key" means. `action` has no key discriminator, so `HOLDER:NAME` is exactly the composite slot the holder set was read from. Holds.
- Every caller passes the composite set or a served subset of it, so the helper never looks up a holder with no composite slot. A disabled holder dropped from the subset gives the same answer the name-only count gave. Holds.
- The docblock paragraph added to `overlaySlotBinding` and the helper's own docblock agree with the code sentence by sentence.
- Attempts to break it: registration order (the binding is read at call time, both orders agree); a bound holder beside an object-less one; three owner keys; the legacy object-less spelling; a scoped package id. None breaks the rule.

Findings:

- nit — the helper reads each holder's composite slot, while the owner-scoped view reads the holder's served item. They agree unless a holder's own stored row carries a different owner key than its artifact. No path to that state was found in this read; a follow-up should confirm a save door refuses it. No change on this head.
- nit — the three older bullets of the `overlaySlotBinding` docblock still state the one-holder rule without the action qualifier, which only the trailing paragraph adds. Readable as is; accepted deviation.

No must-fix and no should-fix. The round ends here.
